name: Sable Freight Long-Haul Cab Driver's Road Rig
description: Independent long-haul freight cab operators — the ones running Sable Freight contracts through the M88 outer corridors, acid-rain bypasses, and inter-sector cargo routes — put together a rig that works for sixteen hours in a cab seat and doesn't fall apart when they have to get out and deal with a breakdown at 3 AM on an elevated causeway. The trousers are Goretek cargo-cut in washed navy, broken in soft over years, with reinforced seat and inner thigh for long sits, a wide waistband that doesn't dig during extended driving, and cargo pockets on both thighs sealed with snap-buttons. A wide webbing belt in black carries a compact multi-tool and a key fob clip. The upper layer starts with an Ironpass-style heavy thermal work shirt in faded olive — flannel-weight synth-cotton, chest pockets with button closures, rolled-up sleeves almost always, with a Sable Freight contractor patch heat-pressed to the left sleeve upper arm. Over this, when out of the cab, goes a quilted vest in dark charcoal with a stand collar — no sleeves, allowing full arm mobility for cargo strapping and vehicle checks, with a large interior pocket on the left breast for a route tablet. Boots are mid-cut moto-style in worn black synth-leather with a side zip, thick lug sole, and a reinforced toe — not steel-capped, prioritizing comfort for the long sit over full safety rating. A worn baseball-style cap in Sable Freight charcoal-grey with a battered brim completes the head, usually worn front-forward, neural port at the rear left accommodated by a stitched-open eyelet in the cap's rear adjustment band.
functionality: Long-duration seat comfort in reinforced trouser construction, multi-tool and key fob carry on belt, tablet pocket in vest for route data, no-sleeve vest for full arm mobility during vehicle maintenance, neural port clearance in cap rear, side-zip boots for fast on-off, contractor patch for Sable Freight route authorization checkpoints
what_it_says: Independent operator. Not a company employee — a contractor, which means slightly more autonomy and slightly more risk. The olive shirt and charcoal vest are personal choices, not issued gear. The Sable patch is the only corporate marker, and it's on the sleeve, not the chest. This person owns their rig, knows the routes, and has opinions about the best acid-bypass to the eastern sector.
manufacturer: Mixed: Goretek (trousers), Ironpass (work shirt), Sable Freight contractor kit (vest and patch), personal boot selection
price_range: Φ190–Φ280 assembled (spread across multiple purchases over time)
story_hooks: A long-haul driver's route tablet — kept in that interior vest pocket — contains the last six months of manifest data for a Sable Freight corridor that's supposed to be logging empty runs; the cargo weights tell a different story.

The driver is the only person who regularly runs a specific outer-sector bypass route at night and has been informally flagging unusual vehicle activity to a contact — when that contact goes dark, the driver realizes they've been feeding intelligence to someone they can't identify.

A Sable Freight contractor patch has been cloned — someone is running a ghost vehicle on the same route authorization, and the real driver keeps arriving at checkpoints to find logs showing they already passed through hours ago.

physical_description.visual_profile: Utilitarian long-haul operator aesthetic — practical, lived-in, purpose-built for marathon cab shifts and roadside repair work. Silhouette is relaxed but structured, reading as competent and weathered rather than fashionable. The layering creates a functional column from cap to boot, with visible wear patterns that signal genuine use rather than styling.
physical_description.fit: Deliberately loose and non-restrictive through torso and hips to accommodate sixteen-hour seated stretches without circulation compromise. Trousers sit at natural waist with slight drop crotch for cab comfort. Vest drapes without clinging, allowing shoulder and arm freedom. Sleeves rolled or pushed up habitually, never tailored short. Overall impression is 'broken in' rather than fitted.
physical_description.primary_material: Goretek synth-cotton blend trousers (fade-resistant, stain-resistant), Ironpass flannel-weight thermal synth-cotton work shirt, quilted nylon/polyester vest with thermal lining, synth-leather moto boots, woven cotton canvas cap with plastic-coated bill
physical_description.texture: Soft and worn through repeated washing and use — fabrics have lost factory crispness and taken on a lived-in patina. Shirt has subtle flannel weave visible. Vest quilting is pronounced, slightly puffy, with reinforced stitching at stress points. Boot leather shows creasing and scuff marks. Webbing belt is stiff but functional.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary: washed navy (trousers), faded olive-green (shirt), dark charcoal (vest and cap). Accents: black webbing belt, grey Sable Freight patch and logo, worn black synth-leather boots. Palette reads as dust-muted, without bright colors or reflective elements.
physical_description.closures: Snap-button cargo pockets on trousers, standard button fly, button chest pockets on shirt, quilted vest with concealed magnetic snaps down front, side zip on boots, adjustable strap cap with eyelet accommodation for neural port
distinctive_features: Sable Freight contractor patch heat-pressed to left sleeve upper arm — faded from sun exposure, slightly frayed edges
Reinforced seat and inner thigh panel on trousers — visible double-stitching, slightly different fabric tone from repeated stress washing
Wide non-cutting waistband on trousers — custom ergonomic design for sitting comfort
Large interior left-breast pocket on vest — sized for standard route tablet, reinforced with topstitching
Black webbing belt with compact multi-tool clip and key fob attachment — worn smooth from repeated use
Neural port accommodation eyelet on cap rear adjustment band — stitched open, showing deliberate modification for augmentation access
Rolled or pushed-up sleeves habit-worn into fabric with visible creases
Moto-style boot side zip with reinforced toe but no steel cap — comfort-first safety compromise
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3-4 working class — functional contractor kit, not welfare-grade salvage, but definitively non-luxury. Sable Freight contract branding signals independent operator, not full-corpo employment. Repairs and modifications are personal, not professional tailoring.
physical_description.cultural_context: Identifies as long-haul freight independent, likely running GLMZ outer-zone cargo routes. Neural port presence suggests minimal to moderate augmentation — navigation assist or communication implant standard for routing. Not military, not corpo office tier, not street-level sub-grade. Road culture, reliability-focused, self-reliant. Wearing this says: 'I run cargo through the outer corridors at 3 AM and I know how to fix my rig when it breaks.'
physical_description.condition_typical: Thoroughly broken in and worn. Not pristine, not destroyed. Fabrics are soft from washing, colors are faded from sunlight exposure and repeated wear. Boots show creasing and scuff marks. Patch has visible wear and sun-fade. Stitching is intact but thread has dulled. No tears or major damage — that would mean replacement — but weathering is comprehensive and visible. Looks like it has logged thousands of hours in a cab.

image_prompt: Weathered long-haul freight operator standing three-quarter against the side of a battered cargo vehicle in pre-dawn darkness, sodium-vapor lighting casting orange-yellow across worn synth-leather jacket and faded navy cargo trousers. Sable Freight patch visible on left sleeve, worn black moto boots planted on oil-stained concrete, neural port accommodation visible at rear of charcoal cap. Quilted vest unbuttoned revealing faded olive flannel shirt, sleeves pushed up past elbows. Webbing belt with tool clip catching light. Rain-slick causeway and elevated industrial structures blur in background. Moody, utilitarian, photojournalistic framing emphasizing lived-in texture and functional purpose over style. Atmospheric GLMZ outer-zone industrial zone, gritty and authentic. --ar 2:3 --v 6
